extracted.intended_audience: permit applicants, CO2 pipeline developers, Class VI UIC applicants, state and federal regulators, and stakeholders participating in EPA rulemaking or commenting on CCS project permitting
extracted.subtask_short: UIC Class VI permitting for CO2 sequestration
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory and technical requirements for permitting CO2 geologic sequestration (UIC Class VI) and associated CO2 transport infrastructure, including area-of-review modeling, monitoring, seismicity assessment, protection of underground sources of drinking water, and pipeline safety/siting/permit coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: UIC Class VI permit authorization and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: UIC regulations for Class VI wells authorize the injection of CO2 for geologic sequestration while protecting human health by ensuring the protection of underground sources of drinking water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major components to be included in UIC Class VI permits are detailed in section VII.C.1.a.i(D)(4) (referenced). See EPA Class VI permit materials and permit trackers for examples and lists of permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area of review delineation (40 CFR 146.84(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 40 CFR 146.84(a), the area of review is the region surrounding the geologic sequestration project where USDWs may be endangered by the injection activity, and it is to be delineated using computational modeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The modeling must account for the physical and chemical properties of all phases of the injected carbon dioxide stream and be based on available site characterization, monitoring, and operational data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action for existing wells in the area of review
rubrics_metrics.description: UIC permitting authorities may require corrective action for existing wells within the delineated area of review to ensure protection of underground sources of drinking water (USDWs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrective actions are imposed as needed based on the area-of-review modeling and site-specific information to mitigate any pathways that could endanger USDWs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on movement of fluids into USDWs (40 CFR 144.12(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal regulation prohibits the movement of fluid into underground sources of drinking water (USDWs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits and project designs must ensure injected fluids (including CO2 and any associated phases) will not migrate into USDWs in violation of 40 CFR 144.12(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class VI injection well construction requirements (40 CFR 146.86(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Class VI injection wells must meet specific construction requirements set out in the CFR (e.g., 40 CFR 146.86(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate that well construction will meet regulatory standards to protect USDWs; see the Class VI implementation manual for detailed construction expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class VI injection well operation requirements (40 CFR part 146)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational requirements for Class VI wells are codified in 40 CFR part 146 and require ongoing compliance during injection operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operation requirements include monitoring, reporting, well integrity management, and other operational controls; applicants should consult the specific regulatory text and EPA guidance documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency and remedial response requirements (40 CFR 146.94)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations require emergency and remedial response measures for Class VI injection wells (40 CFR 146.94).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits and operators must include plans and capabilities for emergency response and remedial actions to address leaks, unintended migration, or other incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seismicity assessment and demonstration of containment (40 CFR 146.82(a)(3)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations require submission of information on seismic history, including the presence and depth of seismic sources, and a determination that seismicity would not interfere with containment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide site-specific seismic characterization and analyses demonstrating that induced or natural seismicity will not compromise containment. EPA implementation manual and NRC/GWPC guides on induced seismicity are relevant references for methods and considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and characterization of confining zone (40 CFR 146.3 definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Confining zone" means a geological formation, group of formations, or part of a formation that is capable of limiting fluid movement above an injection zone (40 CFR 146.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits and site characterizations must identify confining zones and demonstrate their capacity to limit upward fluid movement; proper characterization is essential to protect USDWs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) plan standards and technical review
rubrics_metrics.description: MRV plans for geologic sequestration projects (e.g., Subpart RR MRV plans) are subject to EPA technical review, as shown by decisions for projects such as Petra Nova, ADM, Red Trail Energy, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MRV plans must meet EPA criteria for monitoring methods, reporting formats, verification approaches, and data sufficiency; EPA technical review decisions provide examples of acceptability and required plan components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequestration site selection and storage capacity assessment (distance/proximity considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequestration potential as it relates to distance from existing resources is a key part of EPA's power sector modeling and site selection, using DOE/NETL data and IPM documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site selection and capacity estimates should account for proximity to capture sources, existing infrastructure, and storage resources; see IPM documentation chapter 6 and DOE/NETL studies for modeling approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 pipeline permitting, siting, safety, and regulatory oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: CO2 pipelines are subject to permitting, siting, and safety regulation by PHMSA, DOT, state agencies, and other authorities; PHMSA has undertaken rulemaking to strengthen oversight in light of increased CO2 pipeline activity and past incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/owners must engage with federal and state authorities, follow PHMSA guidance and any new rulemaking, and be aware of agency letters clarifying jurisdiction. Referenced materials include PHMSA reports, failure investigations, NARUC reports, and state regulatory resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipeline engineering and project timeline considerations (diameter, recompression, construction timelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pipeline engineering choices (e.g., diameter sizing) can be used to avoid recompression stages; EPA representative timelines (and industry permitting guidance) inform realistic construction schedules and permitting durations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting may take ~1.5 years in some analyses; EPA scenarios assumed an 18-month construction period for representative pipelines, but real projects may be spread over longer periods. Design choices should consider recompression needs, permitting schedules, and potential compliance extensions for delays outside operator control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with related federal regulatory authorities and parts (40 CFR parts 124, 144-147 and other federal statutes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carbon sequestration projects may implicate multiple federal authorities — see 40 CFR parts 124 and 144-147 — and other agency regulations and statutes compiled in EPA's Regulatory and Statutory Authorities document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project proponents must identify which authorities apply to their specific circumstances and comply with procedural and substantive requirements across statutes and agency rules; EPA's cross-reference table and CEQ/DOI/BSEE/FAST-41 materials are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of induced seismicity guidance and practical management approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitting and operational planning should incorporate practical approaches to minimizing and managing potential injection-induced seismicity, drawing on NRC, GWPC, and EPA guidance documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References include the National Research Council report on induced seismicity, the GWPC/IOGCC Potential Induced Seismicity Guide, and EPA documents on minimizing/managing induced seismicity; these sources inform monitoring triggers, mitigation measures, and operational controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of federal permitting coordination mechanisms (FAST-41, permitting dashboard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal infrastructure projects, including CCS-related transport and sequestration, may use FAST-41 coordination and the federal Permitting Dashboard to streamline and track permitting and interagency coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA and other agencies provide FAST-41 fact sheets and coordination pages; applicants should consider these mechanisms for schedule management and interagency engagement.
